text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use spread across all complexity tiers, with documentation too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not confined to sick patients: the provider's 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity tier, most noticeably among patients with zero chronic conditions, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include simple-sounding diagnoses such as Z09, J06.9, N39.0 and R21 (e.g., C0059105, C0059772, C0059353). That pattern is consistent with upcoding, but the provider also leans heavily on 99214 and sees a meaningful number of 4+ condition patients, so part of the excess may reflect a genuinely complex panel. The records review cannot settle this. Only three 99215 claims were documented and all supported high MDM, including low-complexity C0059809. No notes showed data-reviewed inflation without a lab line. The documentation is therefore too thin to judge, and the clean results do not offset the tier-wide excess. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled 0–1 condition 99215 claims (starting with the Z09, J06.9, N39.0 and R21 visits) to see whether MDM and time genuinely support level 5 there."}
